channel.title: What is your favourite SCP?
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "What is your favourite SCP?" - Hello.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
I really have to put another vote in here for SCP-3999. That SCP single-handedly convinced me that there's something special going on here on the wiki, and that I wanted to be part of it.

It's strange too, because it's one of the few SCPs where the particulars don't really matter. You could cut a lot from or add a lot of stuff to the first half, and it wouldn't change much. It's not some masterclass in carefully crafting the perfect word-by-word story. Yet, it has had more of an effect on how I consume fiction than any other piece of fiction.

I read it at first, and honestly tried my hardest to hate it. I tried to think that it was pretentious nonsense. But, eventually…

SCP-3999 won.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded: It's really close for me. SCP-3000 and SCP-5001 were some of my first ventures into the foundation and will always hold a special place in my heart. SCP-049 is one of my favorites as well. However, I'd have to say my absolute favorite that I've read so far is SCP-3001.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded: SCP-093 will always be my classic favorite. I really love "exploration" type story driven SCP's and the red sea object is probably the first one to grab my attention. I still don't understand why the author decided to write such a complex story for what was at the time a small creepypasta spinoff site.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded: Id have to say 4999, mainly because it was the first article I read that gave a very different ominous(not in a bad way) visual. To show that however hard they try the Foundation truly can't capture all that is considered "part of the unknown, that there are simply some anomalies that cannot be secured, contained, or protected whether a danger is present or not.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
SCP-035

Its a highly dangerous SCP, but just how much so is not directly obvious. I find its psychological control over humans interesting. It has spent millennia experiencing human society. Now it has seen everything. Every neurosis, every fear, every form of irrationality that we all suffer from to one degree or another. Following lifetimes of practice, it knows exactly how to use this knowledge to further its own narcissistic agenda.

It also can't just be locked away and forgotten. It does not rip through walls like 682 or snap necks in an instant like 173, but it has ways to make containing it near impossible. Whatever the Foundation is doing to control it, it is wearing away its containment and scheming its next move. Insidious and tireless.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded: SCP-2000 is mine. It tackles an extremely difficult concept with a large amount of technobabble, but yet manages to create an interesting and engaging read. In addition, it’s also one of the few SCPs with reread value; every time I read it, I pick up on another subtle detail that I missed the last time.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded: 999 is one that really holds a special place in my heart, especially since I headcanon New Job. I just want to hug it. I want to cuddle it. The idea that it will someday be the undoing of one of the most powerful forces in the SCP 'verse is just icing on the cake.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
I'm down to two: SCP-835 and SCP-2006. 2006 is an incredible article that represents the best of what the site has to offer in an easily digestible piece of fiction (plus we have the same taste in movies), but goddamn 835 is some fucking phenomenal and evocative writing. I start that article as horrified as I can possibly be and then things get ten thousand times worse the further I get. Gears + Clef = amazeballs.

I'd list honorable mentions but they would go on for about three pages.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
SCP-1160

I love how this article handles the problem of an entity that gets more powerful the fewer people know about it by having the SCPF turn the monster into a cereal mascot. Its creative. Its original. It turns the hush hush world of the Foundation containing something on its head, and I just adore that.

item.title: Re: What is your favourite SCP?
item.content:encoded:
As of now it's SCP-2137, the 2Pac CD.

I just really love how it's Keter, but not in the same sense that 682 or 231 are Keter. It doesn't pose a physical threat to the foundation or the world, but a threat to the secrecy of the Foundation.

I also love that technically all the SCP wants, at least for now, is justice for unsolved murder cases, which isn't exactly a bad thing.
